approach: Part (1) is already in the base: model.json:10 has `reopened` as kind "waiting", model.json:110 has t12 reopened -> queued, intro.json:54 (lead-in) and :115 (glossary) say only Done ends the task and reopened goes back to Queued, and commit 30642c0 (HISTORY.txt:633, CHANGELOG.md:987) records it. So model.json and intro.json need no text edit. The one study fault left is claims.json c45 (:345-350), which cites bin/fm-teardown.sh lines 3894-3896 with the quote "Queued" while every other citation of that file is at line 184 or earlier; the plan makes its re-citation an expected deliverable behind a required host gate. Part (2) is the real work. (a) pin.rs gets a small additive field, `SourceReport.findings: Vec<SourceProblem>` (file, kind, statement, evidence), built from the checker's typed problems; `problems` is unchanged. The checker's `file` is normalized against the study's real page-text names (strip a leading `page-text/`, require a name in `study.files`), and one that does not match becomes study-level (`file: None`), so no invented path is queued. (b) steward.rs adds `SourceFinding`, `source_fix_request` (builds through `StewardRequest::new`), `open_requests` and `citing_request`. The dedupe key is a marker line `Source finding: <path> (<kind>)` where path is `studies/<name>/<file>` or `studies/<name>/`; wording never enters the key. (c) drain.rs `Check` carries findings; `RealSteps::check_page` maps `SourceReport.findings` and the model-free floor's contradictions to them (no string parsing); two `Steps` hooks (`open_requests`, `queue_request`) have inert defaults and `RealSteps` implements them with `steward::open_requests` and `Athena::queue`; `Drain::rate` queues one request for the findings no open request cites. In production the request is on channel `cli`, so the re-read of `steps.queue()` after each wave (drain.rs:3084) picks it up and works it in the same run.

decisions.choice: Carry structured findings out of the checker: add `SourceProblem { file: Option<String>, kind, statement, evidence }` and `SourceReport.findings` to pin.rs, filled in `check_study_text_inner` from the typed `CheckerProblem` list. `problems` strings are built exactly as before. drain.rs does no string parsing.
decisions.reason: Answers findings 3 and 2. The typed data already exists at pin.rs:485-494 and printing it to a string and parsing it back is the more fragile path. The file normalization needs `study.files`, which is in scope only there. The change is additive: SourceReport is built only by `check_study_text` (pin.rs:381) and read only at drain.rs:4711, so nothing else changes. pin.rs is added to the deliverables for this reason.

rejected.option: Parse the problem strings in drain.rs with a shape matcher
rejected.why: Fragile (a statement may hold `" (`), and the normalization of the checker's file field would need the study's file list there too. The brief's file list is not the limit, since steward.rs and claims.json are already deliverables.

rejected.option: Keep pin.rs out on scope grounds
rejected.why: Weak: the plan already touches files beyond the request's list, and the field is small and additive.

decisions.choice: Normalize the checker's `file` in a pure function `page_file(study: &StudyText, reported: &str) -> Option<String>` in pin.rs: trim, strip one leading `./`, strip one leading `page-text/`, then return the name only if it equals a `study.files` name; otherwise None. A finding with None is study-level: marker path `studies/<name>/` (a directory path, which `StewardRequest::new` accepts when it ends with `/`, steward.rs:529), and the request's Files line names that directory.
decisions.reason: Answers finding 2. The prompt lists files as `page-text/<name>` (pin.rs:336) and says every problem names its file 'as listed above' (pin.rs:355), but only `files_checked` is compared (pin.rs:496) and `p.file` is unchecked. The same fault could be reported as `model.json` on one run and `page-text/model.json` on the next, which would give two markers and a second request. After normalization both give `studies/demo/model.json`. An unknown name never becomes a path in the request.

rejected.option: Use the checker's file verbatim in the marker
rejected.why: Lets the same fault queue twice and puts a path that does not exist on the Files line.

rejected.option: Leave a finding with an unknown file out of the request
rejected.why: A real contradiction would be reported on every drain and never fixed, which is the defect being fixed.

decisions.choice: The dedupe key is a marker line `Source finding: <path> (<kind>)` written into the request body. A finding counts as cited when a non-Closed request job holds that exact line (trimmed, after `plain_boundary_text`). Statement and evidence wording are never compared. Several findings of one path and kind share one marker.
decisions.reason: For `omitted` the statement is the model's own words (pin.rs:346-347) and for `behavior` a span it picks (pin.rs:352), so it varies run to run; path and kind stay the same while the fault persists. Trade-off: while a request for `studies/x/model.json (behavior)` is open, a second distinct behavior finding in that file is not queued; the drain note names the holding request, and the finding is queued on the first drain after it closes.

rejected.option: Key on the exact statement text
rejected.why: Unstable for omitted and behavior findings; the same fault would be queued every drain.
Still fails when the model rewords the fact and adds a matcher to maintain.

rejected.option: Treat any open source-fix request as covering every finding
rejected.why: Hides a finding in a different file or kind while any fix request is open.

decisions.choice: Queue through `Athena::queue(text)` (reading.rs:919) with the text of `StewardRequest::render()`. The builder, `SourceFinding`, `OpenRequest`, `open_requests` and `citing_request` live in steward.rs. No new commit helper. `Priority::High`.
decisions.reason: `Athena::queue` refuses banned input, redacts, picks a fresh job id and commits the request with the Athena-Job trailer, the same call code_health.rs:763 makes with its StewardRequest text. Channel `cli` is in DRAINED_CHANNELS (steward.rs:342), so the request is picked up. `Drain::rate` re-reads `steps.queue()` after each wave (drain.rs:3084-3090), so in production a fix queued inside `rate()` is read and worked in the same run, within the budget; the duplicate check stops a re-queue if the check fails again (finding 5). This is stated in the module doc and in the CHANGELOG entry.

rejected.option: New `queue_steward_request` writing a Request on the steward channel
rejected.why: Duplicates `Athena::queue`, skips redaction, adds a second commit path.

decisions.choice: `open` means any request job whose state is not Closed (Queued, Proposed, Declined, Dispatched, Blocked). A skipped finding is noted with the citing request's id and state. Statements are quoted inside the request as `statement "..."`, so a structural term in one takes the quoted-or-cited path.
decisions.reason: A running or blocked fix is still an open fix. A stuck request (declined, blocked) shows in the note and in `athena status`; once closed, the next drain queues a new one. The quoted path is covered by corpus case `structural-term-quoted-or-cited-mentions-are-accepted` (refusal_corpus.rs:1316).

rejected.option: Count only Queued/Proposed as open (as `improvement_requests`, steward.rs:376)
rejected.why: A running fix would be duplicated on the next drain.

decisions.choice: Queue findings only for what the page says wrong: the checker's `findings` and the floor's `model_contradictions` (path `studies/<name>/model.json`, kind `model-contradiction`). Not-valid-JSON, checker-did-not-run, file-not-reported, unreadable-study and over-size problems stay in `held_back` only. One request per failed check, at most 10 findings; leftovers are uncited so a later drain takes them.
decisions.reason: Infrastructure problems have no statement to cite and would repeat every drain. One request per failed check is the 'queue one fix request' acceptance; the cap bounds the text.

The new floor test and the site test at xtask/src/site.rs:1019 make the state a checked fact. The c45 re-citation is the study diff.

risks.risk: Claim c45's replacement citation cannot be verified here, because the source is not in the snapshot; a guessed line would fail the source check.
risks.mitigation: The producer edits c45 only with the source mounted and a quote copied from it; otherwise it reports c45 unverified and the host gate stays open, so criteria 1 and 3 do not pass by default. The CHANGELOG states which of the two happened.

risks.risk: The coarse key (path and kind) holds back a second distinct finding in the same file and kind while one fix request is open.
risks.mitigation: Intended trade-off for stability: it is queued on the first drain after the request closes, and the note names the holding request's id and state. Findings of another path or kind are not held.

risks.risk: A fix request that is declined or blocked stays open and blocks re-queueing; a request whose job fails and closes is replaced by a new one on the next drain.
risks.mitigation: Every skip notes the holding request's id and state, so a stuck request is visible. One request per failed check and the 10-finding cap bound the rate.

risks.risk: The checker may report a file name that is not one of the study's page-text names, so the finding is study-level and can sit under the same marker as other unknown-file findings of the same kind.
risks.mitigation: `page_file` returns None for a name outside `study.files`; the marker is `studies/<name>/ (<kind>)`, no invented path is queued, and unit and integration tests cover the unknown name.

risks.risk: Statement text holding a line that starts '- ', '* ' or '1. ', a newline, or a boundary word could make `athena plan` read extra acceptance or admission refuse the text.
risks.mitigation: Every finding line starts with 'Finding N in', whitespace is collapsed to one line, `StewardRequest::new` rewords boundary words and rejects text whose parsed acceptance differs (steward.rs:587), and unit tests cover each form.

risks.risk: Because the fix request is worked in the same run, a fix job that cannot land keeps spending the budget.
risks.mitigation: The job runs under the same limits and reserve as any queued item (drain.rs:3084-3090 rebuilds the plan with the reserve), and the open-request check stops a second request while it is open.

dependents.reason: They describe the held-back report and the budget reserve, which are unchanged. The module doc at line 206 is updated in step 4 to say a fix request is queued and worked in the same run. No test reads it.

demonstrations.method: Read model.json and claims.json, run a new small unit test, and read the git diff for claims.json. The base already satisfies the reopened part, so `git diff` on model.json is expected to be empty; the c45 citation is the diff. The new drain.rs test `the_firstmate_model_returns_a_reopened_item_to_the_queue` includes the real model.json with `include_str!`, asserts state `reopened` is not kind `terminal-success`, t9 goes ready -> reopened, t12 goes reopened -> queued, and `model_contradictions` returns an empty list. It also asserts claims.json c45 no longer cites lines 3894-3896 of bin/fm-teardown.sh. Required gate (host): the cap-study validation test with the source mounted prints `firstmate-work-handling: fully validated`, so every citation, c45 included, matches the source.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes: model.json:10 shows `reopened` as kind `waiting`, model.json:89 t9 ready -> reopened, model.json:110 t12 reopened -> queued, model.json and intro.json unchanged, and `git diff -- studies/firstmate-work-handling/claims.json` shows only c45's source re-cited. The host gate (`cargo test -p athena-cap-study every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates -- --nocapture`, with ATHENA_PIN_URL and ATHENA_PIN_SHA set and the source mounted in pinned-source/) prints 'firstmate-work-handling: fully validated'. Until that gate passes, criterion 1 is not met.
demonstrations.fails_without: If model.json marked reopened `terminal-success`, lacked t12, or contradicted itself, the assertions fail; if c45 still cited lines 3894-3896, the c45 assertion and the host gate fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `drain::model_contradictions` (drain.rs:3426, exists). Fixture: the real studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json and claims.json read with `include_str!`. No fake. The test is added by plan step 8; the host gate uses `check_studies` (crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs:1848, exists) on the real studies/ directory and the mounted source.

demonstrations.method: Run the existing xtask site test that renders the real study and Grep intro.json for `final state`. `reopened_no_longer_carries_the_bare_terminal_success_tag_and_it_is_explained` (xtask/src/site.rs:1019) asserts reopened has no `ends the task` tag and that the page explains it. The lead-in (intro.json:54) and glossary entry (intro.json:115) say the item goes back to Queued and the task is not finished, citing c23 and c45; the citation c45 points to is the one re-cited in step 7.
demonstrations.observes: The test passes. Grep `final state` in studies/firstmate-work-handling/intro.json matches only the `done` term (line 83). Line 115 reads 'The item goes back to Queued for the captain's answer; the task is not finished.' with claims c23 and c45. The criterion is met only together with the host gate of criterion 1, since c45 is its citation.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the glossary or lead-in were reverted to say reopened is the final state or ends the task, the site test or the Grep result shows it.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `render(&real_study())` in xtask/src/site.rs (exists). Fixture: the real study directory. No fake.

demonstrations.method: Two parts. (a) Run here: build the site (reads model.json, claims, intro and renders reopened as `waiting` with t12 to queued) and the floor test of criterion 1. (b) Required host gate: the cap-study validation of every citation without a model call, with the firstmate source at 6407052f4c521e39401ce2305dfa45d201249827 mounted and the two pin variables set; a bad-citation or quote-mismatch for c45 is fixed in claims.json (step 7) and rerun until it passes. (c) The live `athena drain` source check needs a model call and runs only on the host; this plan does not claim it, and the drain's fix-request behavior (criterion 4) covers what happens if it fails.
demonstrations.observes: (a) Exit 0, page written, reopened carries the `waiting` tag, t12 goes to queued. (b) `cargo test -p athena-cap-study every_study_follows_the_conventions_and_the_matching_one_validates -- --nocapture` prints 'firstmate-work-handling: fully validated' and passes. Only (c) shows the model-backed source check passing.
demonstrations.fails_without: If model.json were invalid or lost t12, the site build or the floor test fails. A wrong c45 citation fails only part (b).
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: the xtask `site` command (xtask/src/site.rs, exists) and `check_studies` (crates/athena-cap-study/src/rules.rs:1848, exists). Fixtures: the real studies/ directory and, on the host, the mounted source tree and the two environment variables. No fake.

demonstrations.method: Four layers. (0) pin.rs unit tests: the pure `page_file` maps `model.json`, `page-text/model.json` and `./page-text/model.json` to `model.json`, and `nope.json`, `../x` and an empty string to None; a stub-free test of the finding builder checks the three kinds. (1) steward.rs unit tests named `source_fix_*` cover the builder, the marker, `open_requests` and `citing_request`. (2) drain.rs unit test with `FixStub` (a `Steps` double that stores text only): its `check_page` is the fake source check and returns `Check::fail(..).with_findings(vec![SourceFinding { study: demo, file: Some(claims.json), kind: contradicted, text: the quoted statement and its evidence }])`. Its `queue_request` appends the text to a `RefCell<Vec<String>>` and its `open_requests` returns those texts as `OpenRequest`s in state 'queued'. Run `drain()` four times on one stub: the first queues exactly one request; the second queues none; the third has the same path and kind but a reworded statement and queues none; the fourth has a finding for another file and queues one citing only that finding. A separate test makes the stub's `queue()` return the stored requests and asserts the second wave of the same run sees the fix as a queued item (drain.rs:3084). Assert the stored text starts with 'Priority: high', holds the statement, its evidence and the marker, has a non-empty `request_text_acceptance`, and that `report.notes` names the queued job on the first run and the citing request and its state on the second. (3) Integration in tests/drain.rs `source_check_fix_queues_one_request_then_none_while_it_is_open` runs `drain::drain` over `WithRealCheck` (real `RealSteps::check_page`, `open_requests`, `queue_request`) with the fake checker judge and `WRONG_CLAIM` in a `commit_study` repository. The first drain's judge reports the file as `page-text/claims.json`; `Records::load` then shows exactly one non-closed request job holding WRONG_CLAIM, the pinned-source evidence and `Source finding: studies/demo/claims.json (contradicted)`. A second drain with a fresh stub whose judge reports the bare `claims.json` leaves one; a judge that reports an unknown file `nothing.json` adds exactly one request whose marker is `Source finding: studies/demo/ (contradicted)` and whose Files line is `studies/demo/`, and a repeat of it adds none.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core page_file && cargo test -p athena-core source_fix && cargo test -p athena-cli source_check_fix
demonstrations.observes: After the first drain exactly one request exists, citing the contradicted statement and its source; after the second, still one, even though the file is spelled differently; a reworded statement for the same path and kind adds none; a finding for another file adds one that cites only itself; an unknown file is keyed study-level and never appears as a path. The steward.rs tests show the request is built by `StewardRequest::new`, reads as acceptance bullets, and that a boundary-word or mid-line '- ' statement is reworded and still builds.
demonstrations.fails_without: With no queueing in `rate()` the store stays empty and the first count assertion fails. With no dedupe the second drain adds a second request. With the statement or evidence in the key the reworded drain adds a duplicate. With the file used verbatim the `page-text/` drain adds a second request on the second spelling. Without the normalization the unknown-file case would put `nothing.json` on the Files line.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry point `drain::drain(&steps, limits, &ui)` (exists). Injected doubles: `FixStub` (added by plan step 6) implements `Steps`, including the two hooks that step 4 adds with inert defaults; it stores text only, and the code under test (`Drain::rate`, `queue_source_fix`, `steward::source_fix_request`, `steward::citing_request`) is not in it. For the integration test: `judged_scenario(Arc::new(judge))`, `Fixture`, `commit_study` (tests/drain.rs:6840-6854, exist) and `WithRealCheck` (exists; step 7 adds two delegating methods). The `SourceReport.findings` field and `page_file` come from plan step 1, which pin.rs unit tests cover without a model call.

demonstrations.method: Run the three Athena checks plus the refusal corpus the new request text passes through. The corpus is run as a regression and no case is added: no reading or admission rule changes, and the cases read for the input forms are `dash-bullet`, `structural-term-quoted-or-cited-mentions-are-accepted` (refusal_corpus.rs:1316) and those at 1416, 1425 and 1437.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All exit 0, including the new pin.rs, steward.rs, drain.rs and tests/drain.rs tests, `cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus` (unchanged) and `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` (no prompt text changes).
demonstrations.fails_without: A compile break in any `Steps` implementor, a clippy warning in new code, or a failing new test fails the run.
demonstrations.seam: Whole workspace; no fake. Existing `Steps` implementors (drain.rs 4295, 4865, 4941, 5033, 6281, 7195; tests/drain.rs 292, 1806, 6204, 7106, 7823, 8703) compile unchanged because the new methods have defaults.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG.md diff. One new bullet at the top of '### Changed' under '## [Unreleased]', wrapped like its neighbours, in words not on the boundary list. It states the root cause (a failed source check queued nothing, so one contradiction was reported on every drain), the fix request built through `StewardRequest` and queued with `Athena::queue`, the dedupe by study file and kind against non-closed requests (with the checker's `page-text/` spelling normalized), that the fix is read and worked in the same run within budget, the structured `SourceReport.findings`, the two `Steps` hooks, that the reopened study correction was already in the base (commit 30642c0) and is pinned by a test, and that c45 was re-cited (old and new lines).
demonstrations.observes: One new bullet with all of the above. If c45 could not be re-cited because the source was not available, the bullet says so and the criterion 1 and 3 gate stays open.
demonstrations.fails_without: Admission refuses a candidate that leaves CHANGELOG.md out (CHANGELOG.md:29); a bullet that names a boundary word fails the policy scan in xtask/tests/policy.rs.
demonstrations.seam: CHANGELOG.md, a content check. No fake.
